reviews.text:
If you’re looking for an unforgettable Vietnamese dining experience, this hidden gem of a restaurant is a must-visit. Specializing in both shredded chicken and fried chicken dishes, the menu offers an incredible balance of flavors and textures that capture the essence of traditional Vietnamese cuisine.

First visit I ordered the shredded chicken, and it was nothing short of spectacular. The tender chicken was perfectly seasoned, I was shown how to mix the lime with salt and the dressing added a tangy and savory punch, making every bite refreshing and satisfying.

My next visit, I couldn’t resist the fried chicken.
Crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, this dish is a perfect example of how simplicity done right can create something extraordinary. The chicken was served with a side of salad, orange rice along with a flavorful dipping sauce that perfectly complemented the crispy skin and succulent meat.

The portions were generous, prices are very affordable and the staff were incredibly welcoming, providing top-notch service. The restaurant itself has a cozy, relaxed atmosphere, making it the perfect spot for a casual meal with friends or family.

I have dined in and also ordered takeout on a few occasions, never been disappointed either way.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Vietnamese flavors in a warm, friendly setting!

reviews.text:
While craving banh mi, I stumbled upon this shop along the way. Although the name seemed different from the Google listing, the location and opening hours matched Nha Viet.

We arrived for dinner around 6 pm, and the shop was still open.

Inside, there was ample seating, and al fresco seating was available along the road. However, numerous vendors approached us while dining in al fresco.

We ordered the two recommended banh mi options suggested by the counter staff, which did not disappoint.

The meat was pork and a mix of other meats, if I recall correctly. The meat was tender and flavorful, complemented by seasoned vegetables that enhanced its taste.

Everything was delicious, with crunchy bread on the outside and soft on the inside.

The serving time was fast, and the portion size was reasonable for the price. We also ordered three drinks, all of which were excellent. The options included an avocado shake, mango yogurt, and hot cocoa, none of which were overly sweet. However, the temperature of the hot cocoa was lukewarm, rather than hot, despite my request for it to be extra hot. I suppose this is typical in Vietnam.

Everything else was perfect.

**A must-try banh mi spot in Da Nang**
I had the chance to try the beef sausage (chả bò) and sunny-side-up egg banh mi at **Banh Mi - Bread Thao**, and it was truly a satisfying experience.

The baguette was freshly baked, crispy on the outside, and warm on the inside. The filling was generous and flavorful – the beef sausage was savory and well-seasoned, and the egg added a nice richness. Simple ingredients, but prepared with care and great balance.

The shop is clean and airy, and the service is friendly and welcoming. The staff speak English well, which makes it easy for international travelers to order. Prices are affordable and fair for both locals and tourists.

If you’re in Da Nang and looking for a high-quality, authentic banh mi, this place is definitely worth a visit.

Our 4th wedding anniversary dinner at Le Comptoir was truly a perfect experience.

From our email correspondence before the visit, to the warm welcome we received when we walked through the door, and all the way until we left, every moment was exceptional.

In particular, Myriam Moretto showed an extraordinary level of care and consideration toward my wife, who is 19 weeks pregnant.

My wife was also able to enjoy a wine pairing experience alongside me, thanks to the team’s incredible kindness and patience. Even when I asked several times to confirm that the wine offered to her was truly 0.00% non-alcoholic, they responded with genuine warmth and professionalism.

Although there were some language barriers, every member of the serving team continued to treat us with extraordinary kindness and consideration throughout the entire evening. Their hospitality truly touched us.

The evening ended beautifully with a special “Happy 4th Anniversary” lettering service, making our anniversary dinner absolutely perfect.

If we ever need a reason to come back to Da Nang, visiting Le Comptoir again will be one of the first reasons that comes to mind.

We had a wonderful dining experience at Riverside Terrace Restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious — every dish was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully presented. A special thank you to Van, our waitress, who was incredibly attentive, friendly, and very fast with service. She made sure everything was perfect throughout our meal and always checked on us with a smile. Great food, stunning rooftop views, and excellent service — highly recommended when visiting Da Nang!

We visited this restaurant yesterday. We booked a table in advance via Instagram, and there were no issues with that; they responded quickly. We specifically chose the fourth-floor terrace so we could watch the Dragon Bridge show in the evening. The waitstaff were friendly and tried to resolve issues promptly. That pretty much sums up the positives of the place. My child ordered the Marsala Gnocchi but couldn't finish it; I couldn't finish it either after trying his portion—it was incredibly salty. Then again, I’m just sharing our experience; perhaps some people actually like it that way. We spent a long time choosing a pizza and eventually ordered the Meat Lover Pizza. That was a huge mistake. The pizza was incredibly spicy. I generally dislike spicy food—even just a little bit. There was no indication on the menu that this pizza was spicy, even though other items did have such notes. I urge you to add a spicy label to the menu for this pizza so other guests don't end up as disappointed as I was yesterday (assuming they don't like spicy food, of course). It was a very unpleasant surprise. They offered to replace the pizza with a non-spicy one for free, but the experience was already ruined. They also offered a complimentary cocktail, but we declined; we didn't want anything else at that point. The only good thing about the pizza was the dough—it was actually excellent. Overall, the food was terrible. I would never come back here. I really regret choosing this place.

From the moment we walked in we knew we were going to have a good night. Straight away the owner came over and introduced himself. It was amazing to hear and see how passionate he is about his restaurant and his customers. This restaurant is located with an amazing view of the dragon bridge. Our food did take an hour to come out, however, it was worth it!! The lasagne is amazing! The owner compensated due to the wait time and let us up on the terrace to watch the dragon bridge show! I would recommend booking in advance to get a table on the terrace if you are wanting to see the show as there is limited seating and the restaurant is very busy! I have to give credit to the staff too who were so attentive and helpful.

truly an amazing dining experience. the bruschetta sampler was incredible and recommended to me. does spaghetti and meatballs was also very nostalgic. I finished off my meal with a double espresso and chocolate gelato and both were perfect.

We had the pleasure of dining at this fantastic Italian restaurant in Da Nang city centre and decided to take a night off from local cuisine. It was definitely worth it.

The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming from the moment we arrived. We chose to sit on the balcony. The stairs were a bit of a workout (haha), but absolutely worth it for the beautiful view. We even caught the sunset, which made the experience even more special.

Huge disappointment – the magic is completely gone! ⭐⭐

On our last visit, this restaurant was an absolute gem. It served delicious, authentic Italian food and was run by an Italian owner who played live guitar, creating a truly magical atmosphere.

Unfortunately, the restaurant has changed hands, and all of that magic is gone. The food is okay, but nothing more than mediocre.

There was nothing special about it, and we got some rather boring pizzas where the crust and toppings just didn’t harmonize.

What made it even more disappointing was that we contacted them via WhatsApp three days in advance to specifically confirm if they still had the same owner and live music. They assured us they did, but the reality was a massive letdown. The cozy live guitar was replaced by terrible, loud, "ferry-style" music. The local Vietnamese musicians didn't even know the lyrics to the songs, making the whole experience noisy and distracting rather than atmospheric.

We will unfortunately not be returning, and we can no longer recommend this place to anyone.

We are South African, coming from a country with a large Indian population and a strong love for bold, flavourful curries, so we are quite picky when it comes to Indian food. This meal absolutely delivered as everything we ordered was excellent.

The chicken tikka masala was creamy, well balanced and full of flavour. The chicken was tender and clearly well marinated. The lamb biryani was fragrant and beautifully presented with generous pieces of juicy lamb and a lovely mix of spices. It came with raita on the side which added a nice cooling contrast. The garlic naan was soft, warm and generously brushed with garlic and butter, perfect for scooping up the curries. To finish, we shared gulab jamun, which was warm, soft and soaked in syrup and the perfect way to end the meal.

The restaurant itself has a warm, stylish atmosphere with a lovely bar area and comfortable seating. Service was quick and the staff were genuinely friendly and attentive throughout. The place quickly filled up while we were there and it was just an average Tuesday night. Overall, a fantastic Indian meal in Da Nang and definitely somewhere we would return to and happily recommend.

reviews.text:
Undoubtedly, this is an experience worth trying. And I can say for sure — it’s not for everyone. For people who love Michelin restaurants, it’s often more about the label, where the food frequently does not match the quality that is claimed. Yes, Michelin today is largely a commercial story.

Now, about this place we visited today — this is a story about real quality, about details, which is the most important thing. Yes, details. And for those who are actually able to appreciate them. These details include the service — and I would even say synchronized service — the quality of the food itself, the presentation, and of course the interior and the intimacy. Because intimacy is key here.

There are only three tables on the second floor. We’ve already been here once with friends from our group. And downstairs there are two tables: one for two people and one for a small group. So in total, the restaurant serves only three tables. Just imagine that. The entire kitchen and the entire staff work exclusively for you. Can you imagine that? Yes, you can — in places like this.

This is not for people who love flashy social gold. This is for those who truly know how to appreciate what is offered here. This is my second time at this restaurant, and I’m sure I’ll come back again and again, because now I live in Da Nang. And this is one of my absolute favorite places. Yes, it may not be a place for everyday dining due to the cost, but why not allow yourself such exceptional cuisine from time to time?

From what we ate, my absolute favorite was the lamb. The lamb here is prepared in the best way I have ever tried in my life. And it turns out — I do like lamb after all. In other places, I didn’t. I can say with certainty: this is the best lamb I’ve ever eaten.

As for the steak: it was most likely cooked sous-vide. And it’s simply fantastic. Excellent meat, excellent quality. There is absolutely no sense of freezing and defrosting. Everything is served exactly as it should be. And I’m saying this as someone who lives in Argentina — the country of meat. This is one of the best steaks I’ve ever had in my life. Even better than the ones I cook myself.

Of course, the tartare. The tartare is done beautifully. Everything is correct, with an excellent recipe. This is something that only people who truly love tartare can appreciate. We also tried the seasonal fish. The portion was small, but everything was very flavorful and well executed. And the risotto — truffle risotto — simply brilliant. Brilliantly made, delivering pleasure to every single taste receptor.

In fact, I’ve tried almost everything at this restaurant. We also tried the set menu before. I liked about 70–80% of the dishes in the set menu. Around 20% were just okay. But overall, the set menu is still a very good alternative for those who want to try everything at once. Not everything from the main menu, of course — it’s a separate selection — but it’s a very solid experience that deserves attention.

Now about alcohol. This is definitely the weak point. Some of the alcohol here is spoiled. Some of it, frankly speaking, does not match the level of the food at all. That’s why the second time, we didn’t drink alcohol. And honestly, everything is great even without it.

I understand that Vietnam is not Argentina or France, so wine culture is simpler here. And another reason the wine is spoiled is likely not the restaurant itself, but the supply chain — from producer countries to distributors and then to restaurants. I’ve noticed this not for the first time in Asia: much of the alcohol, especially red wine, is spoiled or sour. Red wine cannot be kept for more than a few hours at temperatures above 22–24°C. That’s something to keep in mind.

Overall, this is an experience that truly deserves attention. And I recommend it to those who are genuinely capable of appreciating it.

As full-time travelers behind our Sunsets & Speakeasies YouTube channel, we eat out a lot, and The Nomad Kitchen on An Thuong 32 seriously impressed us. We showed up hungry—this was our one and only meal of the day—and thankfully, we picked the right place. The space itself is clean, modern, and open, with a relaxed atmosphere that lets the food take center stage.

We decided to share everything, which turned out to be the way to go. The steak was perfectly prepared, with a quality cut and excellent cook. The General Tso’s chicken special was packed with flavor, but the Wagyu Reuben sandwich was sublime. Easily one of those dishes where you take the first bite, look across the table, and immediately know you’re both thinking the same thing. The kitchen team clearly knows what they’re doing—not only with flavor and technique, but with beautiful presentation as well.

We paired everything with two fresh juices and somehow found room to finish with a gorgeous lemon tart, which was the perfect bright ending to a seriously satisfying meal.

The staff were incredible throughout our visit—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Between the professional kitchen team, quality ingredients, presentation, and service, The Nomad Kitchen punches well above a casual neighborhood restaurant.

If you’re staying around An Thuong in Da Nang, put this one on your list. Come hungry, order a few things to share, and do not skip that Wagyu Reuben.

Highly recommended. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Thanks again for visiting us and for the feedback. 🙏
Dani.

Extremely disappointing experience absolutely not worth the hype.
Visited after seeing the great Google reviews and drove around 5 km specifically to have dinner here. Unfortunately, the experience was pathetic from the food to the staff’s attitude.

It tasted like something from a very average local dhaba, not a restaurant with such high ratings.The rotis were equally bad paper-thin, poorly cooked and completely below average.

reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Dear Madam,

Thank you for sharing your feedback. We are sorry to hear that your experience did not meet your expectations.

First, regarding the Paneer dish, we would like to clarify that all our gravies are prepared FRESH every day in our kitchen. We do not use frozen gravy and simply reheat it with paneer added. We take pride in serving freshly prepared food to our customers.

Regarding the roti, our rotis are intentionally thin, which is our usual style (and our naan is prepared in the same style). We do not use yeast or baking powder to make them thick like some other restaurants. This is how we have always prepared our bread, and most of our customers are very happy with it.

During your visit, when you shared your feedback, our staff politely tried to make both of you happy by offering to replace the roti and Lachha Paratha that you had ordered. We also have CCTV cameras in the restaurant, so the interaction can be reviewed. From our side, we genuinely tried to assist you and did not intend to show any attitude or disrespect.

We serve many customers every day, including large groups, and we regularly receive positive feedback about our food and service. Of course, we understand that everyone's taste and expectations are different, and perhaps we simply could not match your expectations on this occasion.

We respect your opinion, but we also feel it is unfair to judge the entire restaurant based mainly on ONE CURRY and the BREAD. Nevertheless, we appreciate your feedback and will continue doing our best to provide fresh food and friendly service to all our customers.

We are sorry that our food and style were not suitable for your taste, and we hope you have a better dining experience elsewhere.

Regards,
Manvar Rasoi Team

I wish I could give it higher than 5 stars.

Since we started slow traveling, one thing we really miss is having a dog. So we made a special trip to Little Dogs Coffee and Cake Cafe, and let me tell you, it was one of the best decisions we have made in Da Nang!

When we first arrived, we were a little disappointed because there were no dogs around. The owner must have noticed because she went and got the dogs for us! 🥹 That absolutely made our day. They were so friendly and excited to be petted, and we could have spent hours with them. The owner was just as wonderful, taking the time to talk with us and making us feel so welcome.

Honestly, at that point, I didn't even care if the coffee and pastries were any good. We were already having such a great experience!

BUT LET ME TELL YOU... the food and drinks did not disappoint! The salted coffee was easily one of the best we have had so far in Da Nang. We also tried a Vietnamese iced coffee, and we shared a pound cake filled with whipped cream, fresh strawberries, and strawberry puree. The cake was simply perfect, with just the right amount of sweetness to go along with our coffees. ☕🍰

And did I mention the prices? Ridiculously good!

We usually enjoy trying a different coffee shop every morning, but this place is going to be an exception. We are already talking about making regular trips back, getting our dog fix, and trying some of their banh mi sandwiches next time.

This is exactly what I love about Vietnam. It's not just about the food or the places you visit. It's the people, the little unexpected experiences, and the places that make you feel at home even when you're halfway around the world.

I honestly wish we had a cozy, inviting place like this back in Las Vegas. Until then, we'll just have to keep coming back here! 🐶❤️

I came here mainly to work, and the space is definitely one of this café’s strongest points. The interior is clean, minimal, and comfortable, with plenty of seating and a quiet atmosphere that makes it easy to focus. The small outdoor courtyard is also a nice spot if you prefer some fresh air.

Unfortunately, the coffee was a letdown. I ordered an iced black coffee, but the flavor tasted rather flat and lacked the clarity and sweetness I would expect from a specialty coffee shop. Considering their branding, I was expecting a much better cup.

Overall, it’s a decent place to work or have a meeting, but if you’re visiting primarily for the coffee, it may not meet your expectations. Hopefully they can improve the consistency and quality of their brews.

Coffee: 9/10 – the standout feature. The shop roasts its own beans, focusing on specialty coffee with a wide range of bean varieties and brewing methods. Customers particularly praise the cappuccino, pour-over, and Ethiopian/Panamanian coffees.
* Ambiance: 9/10 – spacious, airy, and filled with greenery; the air-conditioned indoor area is relatively quiet, making it suitable for working or studying, while the outdoor area offers a more relaxed vibe.
* Service: 9/10 – generally positive feedback regarding the friendly and enthusiastic staff.
* Price: 8.5/10 – considered reasonable given the quality of the specialty coffee.
* Location: 9/10 – the Truong Thi 6 branch is very convenient for those just arriving in Da Nang, as it is located close to the airport.

Passport Coffee Lab is a truly lovely stop for anyone who appreciates a cozy atmosphere and quality coffee. Right at the entrance, a small bonsai plant by the window sets a calm, earthy tone for the whole space.

The interior is thoughtfully decorated with wooden shelving displaying V60 pour-over sets, books, plants, and charming little trinkets — it's clear the owner put a lot of care and personal style into the design.

The baristas are skilled and meticulous in every step of grinding and brewing, which really shows their dedication to the quality of every cup. The coffee menu here is impressively diverse, with each cup being rich, aromatic, and full-bodied.

The pastries here (croissants, strawberry tarts) are fresh and beautifully presented too — perfect alongside a good cup of coffee.

A lovely little coffee discovery in Da Nang!

I happened to walk past this place and was immediately attracted by the beautiful and cozy atmosphere, so I decided to stop by and take a look. The staff were very friendly and recommended the Lemon Cold Brew, so I decided to give it a try and take it away.

Honestly, the drink was surprisingly good! The cold brew had a refreshing coffee flavor with a bright, slightly tangy lemon taste. It was a really enjoyable drink, especially for a hot day in Da Nang. 🍋☕️

We dropped by for lunch and had the whole place to ourselves because they seem to focus mostly on the dinner crowd. Keep in mind there is no A/C, so it gets incredibly hot during the day. I would highly recommend coming for dinner instead.
The crab soup with greens (Ghẹ nấu rau muống) was excellent. The greens actually tasted more like sweet potato leaves than morning glory. The crab meat was remarkably sweet and fresh, and the broth had a subtle spicy kick that really opened up our appetite.
The seafood fried glass noodles (Miến xào hải sản) featured incredibly sweet pineapple chunks, and the noodles absorbed all the savory flavors beautifully. It came loaded with shrimp, squid, and wood ear mushrooms, making for a perfectly balanced savory dish.
For the salt and pepper mantis shrimp (Tôm tít rang muối), the owner went above and beyond by helping us peel them, which was amazing service. The shrimp were packed with rich roe.
We also tried the lemongrass stir-fried clams (Hến xào). The herbal flavor was a bit too intense for my personal liking, but it came with a complimentary baguette for dipping into the sauce. The bread had a lovely buttery aroma and tasted delicious.
To top it all off, they even treated us to a complimentary plate of watermelon at the end of our meal. Great food and fantastic service.

Among the seafood joints in Da Nang, Be Nu holds a curious place.
It sits in Alley 267 Ngo Quyen. The place is small. It has the feel of the outskirts of Hoi An, or some familiar village back in Quang Nam. A quiet patch of sky hangs over the tables. Low brick walls run around the yard. In the corner, a jackfruit tree bends under the weight of its fruit. Further off, in the neighbor’s yard, a mango tree stands heavy with green fruit, drawing every eye.
The seafood tanks are bright and clean.
By six in the evening, the tables begin to fill. Chinese, Vietnamese, Westerners. They come because of the good words written about the place on the internet.
I ordered the pufferfish stewed with turmeric, mantis shrimp in garlic butter, squid egg hotpot, grilled stingray, steamed clams, and tamarind crab. The food came fast. One dish after another, neat upon the table.
When the bill came, it was just a little over one million dong. Then, you understood why they keep coming back.

My terrible experience with restaurant staff
My family didn't go snorkeling, so we went to the restaurant to rest beforehand and asked for food early because we had children. The restaurant was okay. While waiting, because no one was there to guide us, we sat at a table supposedly set for another group (the table only had bowls and plates, no food yet). We bought some fresh seafood from the restaurant and asked them to prepare it for us. The restaurant prepared the dish and brought it out to us. Suddenly, while we were eating, a staff member (a thin woman with a gaunt face) came out and said this wasn't our table and asked us to move to another table. We agreed, but she spoke very rudely, saying we sat there without asking anyone. I explained that we had already told them we were tour guide Phuc's group, but we didn't see anyone guiding us, and now they were blaming us. Anyway, I just wanted to keep the peace and only asked for food for the children to eat. But no, the restaurant staff made us wait for over an hour, until 1 PM, while other groups who arrived later got to eat first. After our tour guide returned, they complained that we were seated in the wrong place and had an unpleasant attitude (this was relayed by the tour guide).
It's unacceptable for service staff to have such a petty and resentful attitude towards customers. I wonder if the manager or owner of the restaurant is aware of this? But if the owner reads this review, please retrain your staff. In this day and age, you can tell immediately whether a service is good or not. Even if the restaurant caters to tour groups, it's not a monopoly on the island. If the service isn't good, customers can book in advance to avoid the restaurant.

The location is perfect right in the center of the town facing the harbour. 1 minute walk from the ferry dock. Will definitely come back and stay again.

The best part was staying at Cham Corner Lookout. The location is very central in the main settlement, the room was comfortable and we made use of the rooftop terrace. One of the best restaurants in town. We've been to more than 10, and this one is the best for Vietnamese food. The portions are good, and you're getting a nice amount of meat in them, which is something I learned to appreciate in Hoi An as a westerner used to consuming a fair amount of protein every day. Everything is seasoned but not overly so. The food is delicious, in our opinion.

I did have some issues here, though. First was having a hair in one dish. All in all, you should definitely check this place out if you're in the area and want some tasty food. Just bear in mind that nobody is perfect and things happen.

reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you for taking the time to share your experience at Minh's Kitchen. We are very sorry for the incident during service that caused you dissatisfaction and sincerely apologize for any inconvenience.
However, to avoid misunderstandings for other customers, we would like to clarify some information:
Firstly, regarding the burger, it is true that a mistake occurred when the staff WRONGLY BROUGHT THE WRONG DISH TO THE TABLE OF TWO FOREIGN CUSTOMERS, which led you to mistakenly believe that the restaurant prioritized serving foreign customers. In reality, this was entirely a staff error during service, not discrimination. Because the burger had already been consumed by the other table, we COULD NOT RECOVER the dish, so the kitchen had to prepare a new portion for your table, resulting in a longer wait time. Upon discovering the issue, we immediately apologized and promptly addressed the matter.

Secondly, the burger was NOT included in your bill. The restaurant did not charge for this unserved item.

Thirdly, regarding payment, we NEVER requested or forced you to pay before all the food was served. In fact, your family was the one who ACTIVELY requested payment. We explained that the burger was being re-prepared in the kitchen and would be brought out in a few minutes. However, your family insisted on paying. Therefore, we hope everyone understands the context of the situation.

Fourth, recognizing this as a restaurant error, we have PROACTIVELY REDUCED the total bill by 10% as an apology and to compensate for the inconvenience you experienced. This is a voluntary offer from the restaurant and is NOT intended to AVOID RESPONSIBILITY for the mistake that occurred.

Finally, we would like to affirm that Minh's Kitchen DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN VIETNAMESE AND FOREIGN CUSTOMERS. From the moment you arrived, our staff welcomed you, seated you, and served you with the same enthusiasm as all other guests. The order of service depends on the kitchen's food preparation process and unforeseen incidents such as this instance of bringing the wrong dish, and is not based on the customer's nationality.

We always value all feedback and see it as an opportunity to improve the quality of our services. Once again, we sincerely apologize for the mistake that occurred and thank you for taking the time to provide feedback. Thank you for listening.

reviews.text:
The three days I spent at Monkey Homestay were the highlight of my entire trip to Da Nang.

Cham Island is peaceful and unspoiled, making it the perfect place to slow down, relax, and simply enjoy island life. One of the best parts of staying here was the food. Monkey Homestay has, in my opinion, the best chef on the island, using incredibly fresh ingredients. I ordered the crab every day because it was so delicious, the fried rice was amazing, and the fresh orange juice was rich, refreshing, and perfect for the hot weather.

The room was simple but very clean. I especially loved the wooden flooring in the bathroom, and the shower area was spacious and comfortable.

If you’d like to explore the island, you can rent a scooter directly from the homestay. They even fill up the fuel tank for you, which makes everything so convenient.

Breakfast is served downstairs every morning, and it’s one of the best breakfasts you can find on the island. Since the weather gets hot very early in the summer, it’s great not having to go somewhere else just to eat. Waking up and enjoying a delicious breakfast right at the homestay was one of the best decisions we made.

I would definitely stay here again the next time I visit Cham Island.

My family and I had an awesome stay with An and Duyen, the owners of Monkey Homestay and bar. This beautiful family cared for us, feed us and gave us five family stay hospitality. The food was delicious, our boys played with Son.
We will never forget this place and this beautiful family. Thankyou so much for a sensational stay in paradise.
Definitely try the cocktails, fresh Vietnamese black coffee, Banh Mi and avocado and eggs.
Any families planning a trip to Charm Island, off the coast of Hoi An. Make sure you book in with this beautiful family.
